word:hebrew:H1022.explanation: Bêyth hal-Lachmîy means a Bethlehemite, a native of Bethlehem.

word:hebrew:H1057.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to mulberry trees. It is used as the name of a kind of tree, rather than as an action, quality, or person. In the Old Testament, it occurs four times, in two historical accounts from 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles. The word appears within spoken instructions, while the precise significance of each passage depends on its surrounding verse context.

word:hebrew:H1134.explanation: This Hebrew word functions as a personal name, rendered “Ben.” It identifies an individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Bible corpus represented here, it occurs twice, both times in 2 Chronicles 17:7. Its role is connected with other words in that verse, but without the verse text and surrounding context, the clearest supported meaning is simply the person’s name. The name should therefore be read as an identifying designation, not expanded into an additional definition.

word:hebrew:H1178.explanation: Baal-Chatsor is the name of a place.

word:hebrew:H1220.explanation: Betser means gold as dug out. It can also refer to a defence.

word:hebrew:H1259.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “hail,” naming a weather phenomenon rather than a person, action, or place. It is used throughout the Old Testament for hail as something God sends and people experience. The word occurs 29 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, especially in Exodus, where it is repeatedly associated with God’s announced and enacted judgments. Its central meaning remains straightforward: hail, considered as an event or force affecting the earth.

word:hebrew:H128.explanation: Adamah is the Hebrew name rendered “Adamah.” It functions as a specific name rather than a general description or action word. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at Joshua 19:36, and no broader range of uses is represented here. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the lexical item itself identifies “Adamah.”

word:hebrew:H1295.explanation: Berêkâh means a reservoir or pool.

word:hebrew:H1426.explanation: Gaddi is a personal name, preserved as “Gaddi” in English. It does not function as a general descriptive word or action term; it identifies an individual. In the Hebrew Old Testament, this name occurs once, in Numbers 13:11. The available wording does not provide a broader lexical definition beyond the name itself, so its ordinary meaning is simply the personal designation Gaddi. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and verse text.

word:hebrew:H1484.explanation: Gôwr means a whelp, or young lion.

word:hebrew:H1541.explanation: Gelah means to bring over or carry away. It can also mean to reveal.

word:hebrew:H164.explanation: Ehud is a personal name used for Israelites.

word:hebrew:H1699.explanation: Dober means a pasture or fold for a flock. It can also describe manner.

word:hebrew:H1707.explanation: Dabbesheth means a sticky mass, specifically the hump of a camel.

word:hebrew:H1772.explanation: Dayah means a falcon and can also refer to a vulture.

word:hebrew:H1800.explanation: Dal means weak. It can also describe someone poor. It can also describe someone needy.

word:hebrew:H1879.explanation: Dashen means fat; figuratively, it can describe what is rich.

word:hebrew:H2092.explanation: Zaham means to loathe or abhor.

word:hebrew:H2131.explanation: Ziqah means a flash of fire, like a spark. It can also mean a bond or chain.

word:hebrew:H2243.explanation: Chôb means bosom, a close place where something may be hidden.

word:hebrew:H2306.explanation: Chadi means breast, referring to the chest.

word:hebrew:H2409.explanation: This Hebrew word means “sin” and functions as a noun, naming sin rather than describing an action. In the Hebrew Bible data here, it occurs once, in Ezra 6:17. That single occurrence identifies its basic lexical sense, while the surrounding verse would be needed to explain its particular force there. It should therefore be understood simply as the biblical term “sin” in this Hebrew occurrence, without adding meanings that the available information does not establish.

word:hebrew:H2470.explanation: Chalah means to be sick or become weak. It can also mean to entreat, as in asking for someone’s favor.

word:hebrew:H2513.explanation: Chelqah can describe something smooth. It can also refer to a portion or parcel of land.

word:hebrew:H2654.explanation: Chaphêts means to desire something, take delight in it, or be pleased with it. It can describe delight in a person or desire for truth.

word:hebrew:H2702.explanation: This Hebrew word is a place name, rendered “Hazar.” It identifies a location rather than describing an action, quality, or person. The word occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both occurrences appearing in 1 Chronicles 4:31. Because the surrounding verse text is not included here, the name’s particular significance in that list should be understood from its wider context. Its normal function is to designate the named place Hazar. [p03:word:hebrew:H2702:renderings] [p03:word:hebrew:H2702:occurrences] [p01:word:hebrew:H2702:reference:0]

word:hebrew:H2777.explanation: This Hebrew word means “east,” referring to the direction from which the sun rises. It is used as a directional designation rather than as a person, action, or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus represented here, it occurs twice, both occurrences appearing in Jeremiah 19:2. The surrounding verse text is not available here, so its precise sentence-level force must be read from that passage.

word:hebrew:H2838.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “fillets,” a specific kind of band or decorative strip used in the tabernacle’s construction. It names a physical feature of the sanctuary furnishings rather than an action, person, or abstract idea. The word occurs eight times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in Exodus, where it is associated with the tabernacle’s court and its completed furnishings. Its precise placement is determined by the surrounding construction instructions and descriptions.

word:hebrew:H2874.explanation: Tebach means something slaughtered. It can also refer to a slaughtered animal or meat.

word:hebrew:H2997.explanation: Yibnejah is a personal name for an Israelite, rendered Ibneiah in English.

word:hebrew:H300.explanation: This Hebrew word is a rare personal name whose specific meaning cannot be established from the available lexical information. It occurs only once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at 1 Chronicles 7:10. Because no gloss, short definition, or translation rendering is available, it is safest to treat the word as a proper name rather than assign it an unsupported meaning. Its precise significance in that verse would require the actual verse text and surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H3132.explanation: Joelah is a Hebrew personal name, functioning as the name of an individual rather than as a general description or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Chronicles 12:7, and the English rendering preserves it as “Joelah.” No descriptive meaning is given for the name itself, so its clear lexical role is to identify that person. Its significance beyond this personal designation cannot be established from the available information.

word:hebrew:H3266.explanation: This word is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Jeush,” used to identify people in genealogical and family records. It functions as a name rather than a descriptive title or action word. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs ten times, including records connected with births and family lines. The name identifies individuals in the descendants of Esau and in later Israelite genealogies.

word:hebrew:H3288.explanation: Yᵉʻâph means fatigue or being utterly exhausted. In one usage, it is rendered “swiftly,” describing Gabriel’s movement.

word:hebrew:H3363.explanation: Yaqa means to become dislocated or be out of joint. It can also describe being alienated or departing. In another use, it means to hang someone up.

word:hebrew:H3381.explanation: Yarad means to descend or go down. It can also mean to bring something down, as fruit was brought down.

word:hebrew:H3594.explanation: Chiun is a name used as a specific designation rather than a general description. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in Amos 5:26, so its meaning is tied to identifying this particular named referent. The available wording preserves it as “Chiun,” rather than providing a broader descriptive definition. Its precise significance in Amos depends on the surrounding verse and passage, but the word itself functions as a proper name within that occurrence.

word:hebrew:H3648.explanation: Kamar means to yearn deeply, expressing a strong inward feeling. It can also describe being black from burning heat.

word:hebrew:H3730.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a physical object called a “knop.” It functions as a noun naming an item rather than an action, quality, or command. In its 18 Old Testament occurrences, it appears mainly in descriptions of the lampstand and its construction in Exodus, where several such objects are incorporated into the design. It also occurs once each in Amos and Zephaniah. The precise force in any particular verse depends on that passage’s surrounding wording.

word:hebrew:H3749.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “compass,” referring to a defined part or feature of a constructed object. It occurs twice in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, both times in Exodus: once in Exodus 27:5 and again in Exodus 38:4. In both occurrences, it functions as the object associated with making or placing something, so it names a tangible element rather than an action or abstract idea. Its precise significance in either verse depends on the surrounding construction instructions.

word:hebrew:H3785.explanation: Kesheph means magic, sorcery, or witchcraft.

word:hebrew:H379.explanation: Ishod is a personal name, referring to a man named “Ishod” in the Hebrew Old Testament. It is not supplied with a separate lexical definition, so its ordinary meaning is the person’s name rather than an explained character quality or action. The name occurs once, in 1 Chronicles 7:18, within a genealogical setting connected with birth or begetting. Its precise significance as a name is not stated.

word:hebrew:H3846.explanation: “Libnites” is a group name for a family or clan recorded among the Israelites. It functions as a proper designation rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The name occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Numbers, where it appears in genealogical or census-related lists. Thus, the word identifies a particular people group within Israel’s family records, while the surrounding passage supplies the details of their place and ancestry.

word:hebrew:H3903.explanation: Lahmam is a proper place-name in the Hebrew Old Testament. It occurs once, in Joshua 15:40, and the English renderings preserve it as “Lahmam” rather than translating it into an ordinary descriptive word. Because no expanded definition or verse text is available here, its secure meaning is its identity as the named location itself. Its precise significance in Joshua depends on the surrounding passage and the place’s role in the list of Judah’s towns.

word:hebrew:H4036.explanation: Magor-mis-Sabib is a symbolic name for Pashur.

word:hebrew:H4094.explanation: Madqarah means a wound or piercing.

word:hebrew:H4230.explanation: Mechuwgah means a compass, an instrument for marking a circle.

word:hebrew:H4249.explanation: Machli is a personal name used for two Israelites. The name appears in genealogical lists connected with Merari and Mushi.

word:hebrew:H4285.explanation: Machshak means darkness or a dark place.

word:hebrew:H4304.explanation: This Hebrew word means “cloaks” and functions as a noun naming a tangible item. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, once in Ruth and once in Isaiah. Because the word identifies an object, it is not describing an action, quality, or person. Its precise significance in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its ordinary lexical sense remains a reference to cloaks.

word:hebrew:H4348.explanation: This Hebrew word means “burning.” It refers to a burning condition discussed in the Old Testament’s examination of skin conditions. The word occurs five times in the Hebrew Bible, all within Leviticus 13, and is rendered with the idea of burning in each occurrence. Its precise force in any individual verse depends on the surrounding wording, but its central sense remains a burning condition identified during the priestly examination described in that chapter.

word:hebrew:H4432.explanation: Molek is the name of the chief deity of the Ammonites.

word:hebrew:H4447.explanation: This Hebrew word is the personal name “Hammoleketh.” It is a name rather than a common word describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs only once, in 1 Chronicles 7:18, within a genealogical record. The available biblical indexing places it as an object connected with birth or begetting, so its role there is to identify a person named in that family line.

word:hebrew:H4515.explanation: Min'al means a bolt and can also refer to a shoe; here it is rendered as “shoes.”

word:hebrew:H4663.explanation: Miphkad is the name of a gate in Jerusalem.

word:hebrew:H4681.explanation: This Hebrew word is a proper name rendered “Mozah.” It does not function here as a general descriptive term or action word, but identifies something by name. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Joshua 18:26, and the available rendering is consistently “Mozah.” Without the surrounding verse text, its specific referent cannot be described further, but its lexical role is clear: it is a named designation rather than a word expressing an ordinary quality, action, or object.

word:hebrew:H4766.explanation: Marbeh means increasing or an increase. It can also describe something great.

word:hebrew:H4788.explanation: Marud means an outcast, or one cast out. It can also refer to destitution or misery.

word:hebrew:H4821.explanation: Mirma is a Hebrew personal name, functioning as the identifying name of a person rather than as a descriptive word. It is rendered “Mirma” and occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at 1 Chronicles 8:10. The available information identifies the name and its occurrence, but does not provide enough surrounding verse text to explain anything further about the person or the passage’s specific context.

word:hebrew:H4924.explanation: Mashman means fatness. It can also describe fertile land or rich food.

word:hebrew:H4968.explanation: This word is the personal name “Methuselah,” referring to a man in the Hebrew Old Testament. It functions as a proper name rather than a general description or action. The name appears six times, chiefly in Genesis 5 and once in 1 Chronicles 1:3, within genealogical records. Its surrounding references connect it with being born, living, and dying, but the word itself identifies the person rather than expressing those events. Scripture’s recorded rendering is consistently “Methuselah.”

word:hebrew:H4986.explanation: Metheq means sweetness or pleasantness in speech. It can describe the pleasing quality of a person's counsel.

word:hebrew:H5017.explanation: This Hebrew word means “prophesying”—the activity of prophesying. It functions as a verbal expression, describing what someone is doing rather than naming a person or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Ezra 6:14. Its precise role in that sentence depends on the wording and surrounding passage of Ezra 6:14, since the verse text is not included here.

word:hebrew:H5062.explanation: Nagaph means to strike or smite. It can also describe hurting someone or being defeated in battle.

word:hebrew:H5219.explanation: Nekoth means aromatic gum or spicery.

word:hebrew:H5260.explanation: Nesak means to pour out a libation. It can also be rendered offer.

word:hebrew:H5387.explanation: Nasi means an exalted leader, such as a prince or ruler.

word:hebrew:H5516.explanation: Sisera is a personal name. In the account, Sisera is the captain of Jabin’s army.

word:hebrew:H5651.explanation: Ebed is a Hebrew personal name. In the Old Testament, it identifies a particular man rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The name appears six times in six verses: five times in Judges 9 and once in Ezra 8. Its occurrences also appear in passages containing speech about or involving Ebed, but the surrounding verse text is needed to explain each specific scene. The English Bible renderings consistently preserve it as “Ebed.”

word:hebrew:H5725.explanation: Adullam is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H573.explanation: Amittai means an Israelite. Scripture identifies Amittai as Jonah’s father.

word:hebrew:H5790.explanation: Uth means to hasten or help. It can describe speaking a timely word to someone who is weary.

word:hebrew:H5853.explanation: This Hebrew word identifies a place named “Addar” or “Ataroth.” It functions as a proper name rather than a description of an action, quality, or person. The name occurs four times in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, all in Joshua, where it appears in descriptions of territorial boundaries. The two approved English renderings preserve the same place-name while reflecting a spelling variation in translation.

word:hebrew:H5905.explanation: This word refers to a named place, rendered “Irshemesh.” It functions as a proper place-name rather than as an ordinary action, quality, or object word. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs twice, both times in Joshua 19:41, within the description of territory. Since no fuller descriptive definition is available here, the safest meaning is the place-name itself: “Irshemesh.” Its exact significance in that verse belongs to the surrounding territorial list and context.

word:hebrew:H591.explanation: Oniyyah means a ship or ships.

word:hebrew:H6100.explanation: This word refers to Ezion Geber, a place-name rather than a general object, action, or quality. It identifies a location mentioned in Israel’s journey history and in accounts of royal activity. The name appears 14 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, across seven verses, and is rendered “Ezion” and “Geber.” Its precise significance in any particular passage comes from the surrounding account, but its basic function is to identify this place.

word:hebrew:H6179.explanation: Eri is a Hebrew personal name, preserved in English as “Eri.” It identifies an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general object. The name appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, once in Genesis 46:16 and once in Numbers 26:16. Its significance here is the person’s name itself, not a translated concept. The surrounding verse context would be needed to explain each mention.

word:hebrew:H6261.explanation: This Hebrew word means “fit,” describing someone regarded as suitable for a particular task or purpose. It occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in Leviticus 16:21, so its ordinary sense is known from that single use rather than from a broad range of passages. As an adjective-like description, it identifies suitability rather than naming an object, action, or emotion. The surrounding verse supplies the specific role being described, while the word itself contributes the basic idea of being fit.

word:hebrew:H6283.explanation: Athereth means abundance or copiousness. It describes peace and truth present in abundant measure.

word:hebrew:H6328.explanation: Pûwq means to waver. It can describe stumbling or moving.

word:hebrew:H6364.explanation: Pi-Beseth is the name of a place in Egypt.

word:hebrew:H6456.explanation: Pesil means an idol. It can also refer to a carved or graven image.

word:hebrew:H656.explanation: Aphes means to disappear or cease. It can describe money that fails or is gone.

word:hebrew:H6575.explanation: Parashah means an exposition, expressed here as a declaration. It can also refer to a sum.

word:hebrew:H6629.explanation: Tsôʼn means a flock of sheep.

word:hebrew:H6650.explanation: Zeboim is a proper place name, rendered “Zeboim” in English. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, once in 1 Samuel 13:18 and once in Nehemiah 11:34. Because it functions as a name rather than an ordinary descriptive word, its meaning is chiefly its identification of a particular place. The available references do not provide enough surrounding verse text to explain the location or significance further. Its precise role in either passage depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H6791.explanation: Tsên means a thorn or thorns.

word:hebrew:H6834.explanation: Tsippor is a Moabite personal name, rendered Zippor.

word:hebrew:H6878.explanation: This Hebrew word means “need.” It refers to something required or lacking, functioning as a noun rather than describing an action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 2 Chronicles 2:16, so its normal lexical sense is clear but its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording. The English rendering “need” supports this basic meaning for readers.

word:hebrew:H6896.explanation: This Hebrew word means “maw,” naming a bodily part. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at Deuteronomy 18:3. In its recorded use, it functions as the object of actions involving giving and slaughter, identifying the particular part being handled or given rather than describing an action or quality. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H6922.explanation: Qaddîysh means a holy one. It can also refer to the saints of the Most High.

word:hebrew:H6957.explanation: Qav means a line or cord used for measuring.

word:hebrew:H7068.explanation: Qin'ah means jealousy or envy. It can also mean zeal, as in zeal for Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H7086.explanation: Qe'arah means a bowl or dish; it is also rendered as a charger.

word:hebrew:H7121.explanation: Qara means to call out or address by name. It can also describe calling people, as Joshua called twelve men.

word:hebrew:H7239.explanation: Ribbô means a myriad—an indefinitely large number.

word:hebrew:H7240.explanation: Ribbow means ten thousand times ten thousand.

word:hebrew:H7312.explanation: Rûwm means elevation or height. It can also describe haughtiness.

word:hebrew:H7367.explanation: Rachtsah means a bathing place or washing.

word:hebrew:H7446.explanation: Rissah is a Hebrew place-name preserved in English as “Rissah.” It does not function as a general description or action word, but identifies a named location. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs only twice, both times in Numbers 33:21–22. Since no broader definition or alternate approved meaning is available, its clearest ordinary sense is simply the name Rissah; the surrounding passage supplies any further significance.

word:hebrew:H7503.explanation: Raphah means to slacken. It can describe letting someone go or becoming feeble.

word:hebrew:H76.explanation: Abaʻbuʻah means an inflammatory pustule or eruption. It is rendered as “blains” in an outbreak affecting people and animals.

word:hebrew:H7671.explanation: The word is rendered “Shebarim” and functions as a proper place-name, identifying a location mentioned in Joshua 7:5. It is not presented here as a common action, quality, or theological term, but as the name of a specific place in the Hebrew Old Testament. It occurs only once in this corpus, so its precise background and significance cannot be established from this word alone; the surrounding passage supplies its particular setting.

word:hebrew:H7693.explanation: This Hebrew verb describes a sexual violation directed toward a woman. Its recorded uses place it in situations where a man or a household is connected with the action, helping identify its force as an act done to someone rather than a general feeling or condition. It occurs four times in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Zechariah. Its precise force in each passage depends on the surrounding verse.

word:hebrew:H7745.explanation: Shûwchâh means a chasm, including a pit or ditch.

word:hebrew:H775.explanation: “Arphaxad” is a personal name, not a word that describes an action, quality, or object. It identifies a person in the Hebrew Old Testament genealogical record. The name appears nine times, from Genesis through 1 Chronicles, and is repeatedly connected with being born or begotten within a family line. Its meaning is therefore chiefly identifying: it names Arphaxad rather than expressing a general concept.

word:hebrew:H7789.explanation: Shur means to look at, see, or behold.

word:hebrew:H7994.explanation: This Hebrew word means “cormorant,” the name of a particular bird. It functions as a noun, identifying the bird rather than describing an action or quality. The word occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament: once in Leviticus 11:17 and once in Deuteronomy 14:17. These references place it among the named birds in those passages, while the word’s basic meaning remains the bird itself. Its precise significance in either verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H8054.explanation: Shammoth is a Hebrew personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Chronicles 11:27, and English Bible renderings preserve it as “Shammoth.” No broader lexical definition is provided for this word, so its normal meaning is simply the person’s name. The surrounding verse is needed to identify that individual and understand his specific role in the passage.

word:hebrew:H8102.explanation: Shemets means an inkling. It can also mean a little amount.

word:hebrew:H8270.explanation: Shor means the navel or umbilical cord.

word:hebrew:H8313.explanation: Sâraph means to set on fire or burn.

word:hebrew:H8506.explanation: Tōken means a fixed quantity or measure.

word:hebrew:H920.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, rendered “Bidkar.” It identifies an individual rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 2 Kings 9:25. Because no explicit lexical definition or verse text is available here, its precise significance must come from that passage rather than from a broader recurring usage. The supported meaning is therefore the person’s name, Bidkar, not an expanded concept or description.

word:hebrew:H959.explanation: Bâzâh means to disesteem—to despise, disdain, or treat as contemptible. In one example, Esau despised his birthright.

word:hebrew:H98.explanation: Agam means a marsh or pool of standing water.

word:hebrew:H995.explanation: Bîn means to understand or discern.
